en: The Praise of Mahogratārā: Om, homage to Śrī Ugratārā,
whose fierce fangs are manifest and who possesses the terrible, loud laughter of Rudra!

May Ugratārā protect you— she who wears a garland made of human heads, whose roar is as deep as a thundercloud, who is the sustainer of the people of the three worlds, who holds a sword in her hand, and who carries a skull-bowl in her palm.
O Goddess of terrible form and great roar, who brings about the destruction of all enemies; O Giver of boons to your devotees, protect me, who have come to you for refuge! || 1 ||
O Goddess worshipped by gods and demons, served by Siddhas and Gandharvas;
O Goddess who removes the sin of dullness, protect me who have come to you for refuge. || 2 ||

O Goddess who dwells in the center of all mandalas, who brings welfare to all beings, who is faultless, and who is worshipped by the Siddhas; O Goddess, protect me, who have come to you for refuge! 3.
O Goddess, who abide in a terrible form, the destroyer of all life-breaths, the praised one; O Ugratārā, salutations to you eternally! Protect me, who have come to you for refuge. (4)
O Goddess who possesses a mass of matted locks, who holds your lolling tongue aloft, and who bestows swift intelligence—save me, who have come to you for refuge! || 5 ||
O you who are the form of Soma, the form of the fortress, and the form of the Moon, homage be to you!
O you who are the embodiment of Power, salutations to you; protect me, who have come to you for refuge.
I am dull-witted, I am devoid of power, and I am not capable of attaining You; I am sluggish and of feeble intellect—protect me, who have come to You for refuge.
I am unable to perform bathing, giving, recitation, offering of oblations, sacrifice, or even setting out on a journey; protect me, who have come to you for refuge.
Devoid of power, protectorless, and burdened with every sin, I have no other refuge but you; protect me, who have come to you for shelter. (9)
Gaurī, Lakṣmī, Mahāmāyā, Umā, Goddess Sarasvatī—all these are you alone, O Mother; protect me, who have come to you for refuge. 10.
Having worshipped the Goddess with effort by means of substances such as perfumes and flowers, and even through acts such as binding [the image], one obtains the desired fruit.
The man who recites [this] on the eighth, the fourteenth, or the ninth day attains supreme perfection; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
One who seeks liberation attains liberation; one who seeks wealth attains wealth;
and one who seeks knowledge attains knowledge, such as logic, grammar, and the like.
Having recited this hymn, if a man enters into battle, his enemy shall go to destruction and wisdom shall always arise within him. (14)
Whether in affliction, in union, in calamity, or likewise in fear, for one who recites this auspicious hymn, there is no doubt that it brings well-being. (15)
The Praise of the Illustrious and Fierce Tārā is completed.
